after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=2({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})$ on the disk of radius $3$ centered at the origin.
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {3}^{2}=9\pi .
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}2({(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2})\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}2{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{∬}_{Δ}{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{[\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(\frac{81}{4}-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{81}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{81}{2}[\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{81}{2}(2\pi -0) \\  & =81\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{9\pi }\cdot 81\pi =9.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=4{x}^{2}-2xy$ on the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 3}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=2\cdot 3=6.
$$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{∬}_{D}(4{x}^{2}-2xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}(4{x}^{2}-2xy)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{2}[4{x}^{2}y-x{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{2}(12{x}^{2}-9x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[4{x}^{3}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(4\cdot {2}^{3}-18\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{14}{6} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\text{Area}(D)=2\cdot 3=6.
$$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$

$$

after.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ on the disk of radius $6$ centered at the origin.
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {6}^{2}=36\pi .
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 6,\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{6}\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{6}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{[\frac{{r}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{6}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(\frac{{6}^{3}}{3}-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & =72{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\text{d}\theta  \\  & =72[\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =72(2\pi -0) \\  & =144\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{36\pi }\cdot 144\pi =4.
$$
